# ListViewBase

Header: `winui/ui/collections/ListViewBase.hpp`.

The shared base of [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) and [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview): a scrolling, virtualized, selectable collection of templated items. Each item sits in an item container that draws the hover, press and selection chrome.

The items are either plain strings ([set_items()](#set_items), shown as text by the default template) or an index range that an item template turns into content ([set_item_template()](#set_item_template) and [set_item_count()](#set_item_count)). Only the items in and near the viewport are realized, through the [ForEachControl](for-each.md#uiforeachcontrol) inside the [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) ([repeater()](#repeater), [scroll_view()](#scroll_view)). Report changes to the collection with [insert_item()](#insert_item) and [remove_item()](#remove_item) for strings, or the notify_*() calls for a template's collection. The selection then follows its items and the item container transitions play. The selection mode decides which gestures select. Groups, a header and footer, item click, drag reordering and saving the scroll position are all optional. The class cannot be constructed directly. Create a [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) or a [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview).

The list is one tab stop. The arrow keys move the focused item. In Extended mode, and in Single mode with [single_selection_follows_focus()](#single_selection_follows_focus), the selection moves with it. Ctrl+A selects everything in Multiple and Extended mode, or clears the selection when everything is already selected.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  list = std::make_unique<ui::ListViewControl>();
list->set_items({"Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"});
list->set_selection_mode(ui::SelectionMode::Extended);
list->set_height(240.0f);
list->on_selection_changed([](std::optional<std::size_t> index)
                           { std::println("first selected: {}", index.value_or(0)); });

// A template's collection instead of strings:
struct Contact
{
    std::string name;
};
std::vector<Contact> contacts{{"Ada"}, {"Grace"}, {"Linus"}};
list->set_item_template([&contacts](std::size_t i) {
    return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>(contacts[i].name);
});
list->set_item_count(contacts.size());

window.set_content(std::move(list));
```

## `ui::ListViewBase`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::SelectionProvider`, `ui::ValueProvider`.

The shared base of [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) and [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview): a scrolling, virtualized, selectable collection of templated items. Each item sits in an item container that draws the hover, press and selection chrome.

The items are either plain strings ([set_items()](#set_items), shown as text by the default template) or an index range that an item template turns into content ([set_item_template()](#set_item_template) and [set_item_count()](#set_item_count)). Only the items in and near the viewport are realized, through the [ForEachControl](for-each.md#uiforeachcontrol) inside the [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) ([repeater()](#repeater), [scroll_view()](#scroll_view)). Report changes to the collection with [insert_item()](#insert_item) and [remove_item()](#remove_item) for strings, or the notify_*() calls for a template's collection. ### set_group_keys

```cpp
void set_group_keys(std::vector<std::string> keys)
```

Files the items under group headers, one key per item in item order. The groups appear in the order their keys first appear, and the items keep their order within a group, so items with the same key need not be next to each other. An empty vector ungroups. An item past the end of `keys` goes under an empty key. Indices stay positions in the collection. Only the order on screen, which the arrow keys and Shift ranges follow, comes from the groups. In a [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) with a tile or stack layout, each header takes a line of its own.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

Append focusable elements in tab order, so the [Window](../tree/window.md) can build a flat focus ring over the whole tree. The default pushes this element when [focusable()](#focusable), then recurses into every child [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists. Override it when the ring differs from the children: a composite that is one tab stop pushes only itself, a focus scope stops recursing (see [collect_scope_focusables()](#collect_scope_focusables)), a pager leaves out its hidden pages.

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

### drag_enter

```cpp
void drag_enter(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drop events. [drag_over()](#drag_over) is asked first on the innermost drop target under the pointer, then on its drop targets up the tree until one accepts; every element asked has heard [drag_enter()](#drag_enter) first and hears [drag_leave()](#drag_leave) once the drag is no longer its business. The one that accepted gets [drop()](#drop). A control overrides them; the defaults run the handlers set with [on_drag_enter()](../tree/element.md#on_drag_enter)/on_drag_over()/on_drag_leave()/on_drop().

[drag_enter()](#drag_enter): the drag has come over this element; [drag_over()](#drag_over) follows at once.

### drag_over

```cpp
DragResponse drag_over(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drag is over this element: answer what a drop here would do. Asked when it arrives and at every move. The default runs the [on_drag_over()](../tree/element.md#on_drag_over) handler, and refuses without one.

### drag_leave

```cpp
void drag_leave(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The drag left this element, was canceled over it, or was dropped on another target.

### drop

```cpp
void drop(const DragEventArgs& e) override
```

The pointer was released over this element while its [drag_over()](#drag_over) accepted. What the drop did is the operation it accepted.

### drag_completed

```cpp
void drag_completed(DataPackageOperation result) override
```

A drag this element started has ended. `result` is what the target did (None when the drag was canceled or dropped nowhere).

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### covers_children_at

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

This element's own part of clear_dirty(): clear any part it owns but leaves out of [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) (a parked page, a hidden button), through that part's clear_dirty(). Default: nothing.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

This element's own part of [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.

### collect_scope_focusables

```cpp
void collect_scope_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

The inner tab ring, built when this scope is entered: a scope's counterpart to [collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables). A container that becomes a scope must stop recursing in [collect_focusables()](#collect_focusables) and recurse here instead ([Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander) is the worked example), since a child in both rings would be reachable without ever entering.

Three meaningful answers:
- several elements: an ordinary container scope. [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) cycles them, Escape leaves.
- `this` alone: an item-navigating scope. The control's items are not all elements ([ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) creates its rows on demand and destroys them as they scroll out), so focus stays on the control and [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) is routed to [scope_step()](#scope_step) below.
- nothing: there is nothing inside worth entering. [Window](../tree/window.md) doesn't enter, and the key that would have entered goes to this element's own [handle_key()](../tree/element.md#handle_key). That is how Enter expands a collapsed [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander) that is marked as a scope.

The one walk that does not default to recursing through [for_each_child()](#for_each_child): being a scope is something a control opts into, and a default inner ring would make every container enterable while its children still sat in the outer ring too.

### scope_step

```cpp
bool scope_step(int delta) override
```

Move an item-navigating scope's own inner cursor one step: `delta` is +1 for [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) and -1 for Shift+Tab. Wrap and return true to keep focus inside the scope (Escape is then the way out, as for an ordinary container scope). Return false to let the step fall out, popping the scope and leaving focus on this control. Never called for a scope whose inner ring is real elements, since [Window](../tree/window.md) walks that ring itself.

### set_scope_entered

```cpp
void set_scope_entered(bool entered) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md) as this scope is entered (before its inner ring takes focus) and again as it is left, so a control can show and hide whatever inner cursor it draws. A container scope whose inner ring is real Elements usually needs nothing here, since the focused child draws its own focus ring, as it would anywhere else.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const override
```

Inside the item the keyboard is on, cut to the part of it in view. Around the whole list when that item is out of view.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme& theme) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

### focus_ring_inside

```cpp
bool focus_ring_inside() const override
```

Whether the ring goes inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect) in every era, its outer edge on the rect. False by default, which leaves it to the theme. An item inside a viewport (a list row, a tab, a menu item) returns true, as does a control in a tight spot, so a neighbor or the viewport edge never cuts its ring.

### automation_providers

```cpp
void automation_providers(AutomationProviders& out) override
```

Lists what a client can do with this node: set `out`'s field for each pattern this control implements now to `this`, through the provider interface it inherits privately (ui/Automation.hpp). A pattern that only applies in some states is an `if`. `out` arrives empty, and nothing is listed by default.

Example: 
```cpp
class Chip final : public ui::Element, private ui::InvokeProvider
{
protected:
    void automation_providers(ui::AutomationProviders& out) override
    {
        out.invoke = this;
    }

private:
    bool invoke() override
    {
        on_click_();
        return true;
    }
    ui::Callback<void()> on_click_;
};
```

## struct ListViewDragPayload

What a [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) drag carries in [DataPackage::data](../tree/data-package.md): the list it came from and the items dragged.

A drop target reads it back with [`std::any_cast<ListViewDragPayload>(&e.data.data)`](#struct-listviewdragpayload).

Example: 
```cpp
void accept_drops(ui::ListViewControl* left, ui::ListViewControl* right)
{
    right->on_drop([=](const ui::DragEventArgs& e) {
        if (const auto* payload = std::any_cast<ui::ListViewDragPayload>(&e.data.data);
            payload != nullptr && payload->source == left)
        {
            right->insert_item(right->insertion_index_at(e.position), left->items()[payload->items.front()]);
            left->remove_item(payload->items.front());
        }
    });
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `const Element*` | `nullptr` | The list the drag started from (non-owning). |
| `items` | `std::vector<std::size_t>` |  | The indices of the dragged items, in index order. |

## struct DragItemsStartingArgs

The arguments of [ListViewBase::on_drag_items_starting()](#on_drag_items_starting).

The package already carries a [ListViewDragPayload](#struct-listviewdragpayload) in `data.data`. A handler may add text for other drop targets, replace the payload, or return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to stop the drag.

Example: 
```cpp
auto list = std::make_unique<ui::ListViewControl>();
list->set_items({"Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"});
list->on_drag_items_starting([&](const ui::DragItemsStartingArgs& e) {
    if (e.items.size() > 1)
        return ui::Cancel; // single-item drags only
    e.data.text = list->items()[e.items.front()];
    return ui::Proceed;
});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `std::vector<std::size_t>` |  | The indices of the items about to be dragged. |
| `data` | `DataPackage&` |  | The package the drag will carry. [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill) in its text or data. |

## struct DragItemsCompletedArgs

What `on_drag_items_completed` gets once a drag out of a [ListView](list-view.md#uilistview) or [TileView](tile-view.md#uitileview) ends.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `std::vector<std::size_t>` |  | The indices of the dragged items. |
| `result` | `DataPackageOperation` | `DataPackageOperation::None` | What the drop did; None when refused. |

## struct ItemsReorderedArgs

What `on_items_reordered` gets when a drop inside the list moved item [`from`](#struct-itemsreorderedargs) to [`to`](#struct-itemsreorderedargs). Both are positions in the collection after the move.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `std::size_t` | `0` | Where the item was. |
| `to` | `std::size_t` | `0` | Where it is now. |

## Enumerations

### ScrollIntoViewAlignment

```cpp
enum class ScrollIntoViewAlignment
```

Where [ListViewBase::scroll_into_view()](#scroll_into_view) puts the item.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Default` | The least scroll that shows the item. |
| `Leading` | The item at the top of the viewport. |

### ItemsUpdatingScrollMode

```cpp
enum class ItemsUpdatingScrollMode
```

How a list keeps its scroll position while items are inserted and removed.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `KeepItemsInView` | The first item in view stays in view (the default). |
| `KeepScrollOffset` | The scroll offset stays put and the items move under it. |
| `KeepLastItemInView` | A list scrolled to its end stays at its end as items arrive. |
